newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alain Poher, twice French interim president, dies.
newsitem.headline: Alain Poher, twice French interim president, dies.

text.p: Former Senate speaker Alain Poher, who twice stood in as president of France, died on Monday, a spokesman for the upper house said. He was 87.
Poher was acting president for two months when General Charles de Gaulle resigned in 1969 and then again when President Georges Pompidou died in 1974.

The veteran centrist was speaker of the Senate for a quarter of a century after 1968, a job that under the constitution made him the second highest-ranking figure in the country and the interim president in an emergency.
He was last elected speaker in 1989 and retired from politics four years ago.
Poher, a quiet man, made a bid for the presidency himself while standing in for 58 days after de Gaulle resigned. Pompidou defeated him in an election run-off.

"I learned a lot from him. We must not forget that he played a key role in the French Resistance and also in the construction of Europe," said centrist Rene Monory, who succeeded Poher as speaker in 1992.
Conservative politicians said Poher helped counterbalance the power of the Left when it controlled the National Assembly, the lower house, from 1981-86 and 1988-93.

Poher, son of a railway engineer, was born in Ablon-sur-Seine, near Paris, in 1909. After graduating in law and politics, he began his political career in 1946 in the office of then finance minister Robert Schuman.
National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin described him as "a man faithful to his beliefs, a great parliamentarian and an exemplary patriot".
